I have a customer who needs a custom blade made which will be used for shearing granite. They don't know the exact material that their previous tool was made out of so I am attempting to figure it out.

I'm thinking it might be A10 or an S type tool steel, but I can't find anything online that talks about tool steel and granite.

If anyone knows or can point me in the right direction, I'd appreciate it.

Thanks!
Does anyone here know which type of tool steel can be used in shear/splitting granite.
You must be desperate if you're asking here.

Granite in a broad sense has a rockwell B of 7. Tool steels start at about Rockwell C of 50. Carbon steel is a Rockwell B of 60. Pretty much any steel is dramatically harder than granite and will split it successfully. The problem is durability. You want a balance of a hardened edge backed by tempered steel that can give so that the the tool isn't brittle. Jack hammer bits are typically S5 and the business end is oil hardened.

Find out if they have their old blade on hand. Then see if someone locally has a XRF scanner, it will Identify the exact composition and tell you what type of steel it is (4140, 1018, 13-8,17-4, ect). Then do a hardness test to find the temper.

My best guess is that you would want some S type. But I'm no blade expert :)
